A1.justification: Both PDFs describe NoiseQuery and contain complete main texts and Appendices A–C. Text, equations, tables and graphics support reliable comparison, including matching material relocated between the main text and appendix.

before.justification: V2 reports original MSCOCO and DrawBench evaluations, generated-image comparisons, transfer experiments, and sensitivity analyses in the main text and appendices.

after.justification: V3 retains original benchmark and qualitative results and adds quantitative sampler-transfer results in Appendix B.1, Table S2.

M1.justification: Noise-library construction, feature matching, multi-goal reranking and the DDIM-inversion color-offset procedure remain unchanged. The offset explanation moves from Section 4.3 into Appendix C.4 without changing the procedure.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate MSCOCO, DrawBench and the same semantic, visual-property and combined-control tasks. The sampler-transfer addition changes experimental configurations within retained coverage, rather than introducing a dataset or task.

E2.justification: Corresponding comparisons retain Diffusion-DPO, CFG++, ReNO, LaVi-Bridge, Textual Inversion and ControlNet, alongside the same base-model and prompt-based references. The new sampler analysis reuses the base-model-versus-NoiseQuery comparison; the deleted BLIP/CLIP size analysis concerns proposed-method variants.

E3.justification: V3 adds a quantitative DrawBench protocol using a DDIM-built library with SD v2.1 across eight sampler settings. V2's separate 10k, 50k, 100k and 200k library-size sweep is removed. Main benchmark settings and the smaller size/time study in Table 3 remain unchanged.

E4.justification: Appendix B.1 adds quantitative cross-sampler robustness evidence beyond the retained qualitative comparison in Figure S2. Conversely, Appendix B.4 and its BLIP/CLIP library-size sensitivity analysis disappear. Diversity, CFG-scale, model-transfer and complex-generation analyses remain.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, confidence intervals or significance tests. Single-score reporting remains unchanged; the retained DINOv2 standard-deviation statistic measures image diversity rather than estimation uncertainty.

E6.justification: Tables 2, 3 and S1 retain their numerical results. V3 adds sampler-specific scores, such as LMS ImageReward of 0.07 for the base model versus 0.27 with NoiseQuery. V2's library-size results disappear, including the 50k CLIP-query ImageReward of 0.3677 versus 0.3707 for random noise. These are added and removed results under different protocols.

T1.justification: Equations (1)–(4), the finite-step residual-signal argument and the mathematical formulation of noise retrieval are retained. No new formal assumption, derivation or proof is introduced.

C1.justification: The abstract, contribution statements and main conclusion retain the claims of reusable, tuning-free, model-agnostic noise initialization for semantic alignment and low-level visual control. The new sampler results support an existing compatibility claim.

C2.justification: V3 adds explicit limitations: performance remains bounded by the base model, extremely complex cases may underperform, and precise control such as Canny-edge control remains difficult. Removing Appendix B.4 also removes its interpretation of different library-size requirements for BLIP and CLIP queries.

D1.justification: V3 adds a code-repository link in the abstract, absent from v2. Existing implementation explanations and algorithm descriptions remain substantively unchanged, including the retained noise-offset details in Appendix C.4.

R1.justification: Section 2 adds eight cited works, increasing the reference list from 61 to 69, including A Noise Is Worth Diffusion Guidance, Good Seed Makes a Good Crop and Subjective Camera. The existing positioning relative to noise optimization and conditional generation remains largely unchanged.

P1.justification: Most prose and section organization are retained. Local changes include author and acknowledgement edits, an updated appendix overview, removal of B.4, consolidation of the offset explanation into C.4, and a new limitations paragraph.

P2.justification: V2 Figure 10 moves to v3 Figure S4, while Figures 11–12 become 10–11. The library-size Table S2 is removed and a differently structured sampler Table S2 is added. Figure 2 changes columns and the author block becomes more compact; existing graphic contents remain unchanged.

improvement.justification: V3 strengthens quantitative sampler-transfer validation and adds explicit limitations and code-access information. However, it removes the BLIP/CLIP library-size study, including cases where CLIP queries underperformed random noise; retained Table 3 provides narrower size/time evidence. With the central results unchanged, the gain in compatibility evidence and loss of diagnostic completeness leave the net quality direction unclear.
